chunks: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated from Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i, from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Ali ibn Salim, from his father, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about the report that was narrated: ‘Whoever places greater trust in the pledge than in his believing brother, then I am free from him.’ He said: ‘That is when the truth becomes manifest and our Qa'im from the Ahl al-Bayt rises.’

I said: Then what about the report that was narrated: ‘The profit of a believer over another believer is riba’? He said: ‘That is when the truth becomes manifest and our Qa'im from the Ahl al-Bayt rises. But as for today, there is no harm in selling to a believing brother and making a profit from him.’

key_terms.بَرِيءٌ: declared free of or dissociated from
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection
key_terms.قَائِمُنَا: our Qa'im, the one who rises from Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.ٱلرَّهْنِ: pledge or collateral held in a financial transaction
key_terms.ٱلْمُؤْمِنِ: the believing person, especially in relation to fellow believers

ai.seo_question: When does the hadith about profit from a believer being riba apply?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that certain reports condemning reliance on collateral over a believing brother, or profit taken from one believer by another, apply to the time when the truth is fully manifest and the Qa'im of Ahl al-Bayt rises. As for the present time, the Imam عليه السلام permits ordinary sale and profit between believers.
